title: VPC placement heuristics & capacity lab notes
summary: Scratchpad with placement heuristics, quick calculators, and a couple of compact BOM scenarios for VPC/private GPU fleets. Focused on how to split regional capacity, spare policy, and IO/network considerations for latency-sensitive LLM workloads.
body:
Purpose:
Quick working sheet used by the Private Deployments team during Q1 experiments. Not a final procurement doc — more of a lab notebook for tradeoffs and quick scenario generation. Use this to seed more formal proformas.

High-level goals / constraints (short):
- Preserve 99th pctl latency SLOs for interactive routes (chat/generation) while keeping committed spend predictable.
- Target baseline utilization of 55–70% for bursty multi-tenant fleets, higher (70–85%) for single-tenant or dedicated pools.
- Maintain at least N+1 regional redundancy for control plane and model store.

Core heuristics (rules of thumb, distilled from experiments):
- Effective-serving-GPU throughput (tokens/sec) should be expressed per model class (small/med/large). Don't mix in one pool unless compatible latency targets.
- Estimate request token cost = avg_prompt_tokens + avg_generated_tokens. For budget planning, use 95th percentile generated tokens.
- Concurrency planning: assume 60% of peak QPS will arrive in bursts (10–30s). Autoscale reaction time matters; prefer modest overprovisioning (10–20% spare headroom) over frequent scale events in VPC deployments.

Quick estimator (text you can copy into a sheet):
- Inputs (short): target_peak_qps, avg_prompt_tokens, avg_gen_tokens, model_class, p50_latency_ms_target, batch_factor_estimate
- Derived:
  - request_tokens = avg_prompt_tokens + avg_gen_tokens
  - tokens_per_sec_required = target_peak_qps * request_tokens
  - gpu_tokens_per_sec = throughput_by_model_and_hw[model_class] * batch_factor_estimate  # heuristic table below
  - gpus_needed_raw = ceil(tokens_per_sec_required / gpu_tokens_per_sec)
  - gpus_committed = gpus_needed_raw * (1 + headroom_pct) + spare_gpu_count  # headroom_pct: 0.10–0.25; spare_gpu_count: per-region min 1–2

Throughput heuristics table (experimental, units tokens/sec):
- small models (~7B) on 40GB class GPU: 1.2k – 3.5k (use 2.0k for planning)
- medium (~13B) on 80GB class GPU: 800 – 1.6k (use 1.1k)
- large (~70B) on 80–A100 style: 200 – 600 (use 350)
Notes: these are ballpark and vary strongly with sequence length + kv-cache hit rates (prefix caching can multiply effective throughput).

Placement matrix (how to split across regions and AZs):
- Primary factor: customer latency SLOs and regional user distribution.
- Rule: 80/20 split: if >20% traffic from a region -> put a primary pool there. Otherwise use edge-cache + fallback to nearest region.
- Minimum regional pod: 2 racks (~8–16 GPUs depending on node size) to avoid single-rack failure modes.
- Cross-region fallback: keep a warm standby (5–15% capacity) in at least one secondary region if legal/data residency allows.

Spare and spare rotation policy (practical):
- Cold spare (replacement HW) vs hot spare (instant live): prefer hot spare policy inside each primary region when latency-critical. That means ~1–2 hot GPUs per 50 committed GPUs.
- Spare nodes should be on different power/pdu chain and ideally separate racks.
- Replacement SLA: target RMA/ship T+3 days for cold spares, local swap day+1 for hot-swap agreements with suppliers.

Networking / IO considerations (notes):
- Per-GPU network egress: estimate 0.1–0.6 Gbps per active request depending on token size and model. Heavy batching increases egress efficiency.
- Model artifacts (weights) size matters for startup: plan for pre-warmed local disk or mounted fast NVMe to avoid network-model-pull spikes.
- Keep model pull concurrency capped (e.g., 2–4 parallel loads per node) to avoid saturating remote object storage during rollout.

BOM mini-scenarios (two compact examples — back-of-envelope):
Scenario A: regional small-medium mix for a SaaS customer- Assumptions: target_peak_qps=500, avg_prompt=32 tokens, avg_gen=64 tokens, mix: 60% small(7B)/40% med(13B), batch_factor_estimate=1.8, headroom_pct=0.15- Calculation (sketch): request_tokens=96 -> tokens/sec_required=48k- Weighted gpu_tokens_per_sec ~ 0.6*2000 + 0.4*1100 = 1640- gpus_needed_raw = ceil(48000 / (1640*1.8)) ≈ ceil(48000 / 2952) ≈ 17- with headroom 15% + 2 hot spares -> gpus_committed ≈ 17*1.15 + 2 ≈ 22- BOM: 2 racks x 10 GPUs (10x A40-style nodes) -> plan orders in tranches: 10,10,5 to stagger procurement and allow tuning

Scenario B: single-tenant enterprise with high-quality generation (large models)- Assumptions: target_peak_qps=60, avg_prompt=64, avg_gen=512, model_class=large(70B), batch_factor=1.2, headroom=0.20- request_tokens = 576 -> tokens/sec_required = 34,560- gpu_tokens_per_sec=350 -> per-gpu effective with batch=1.2 -> 420- gpus_needed_raw ≈ ceil(34560 / 420) ≈ 83- committed with 20% headroom + 4 hot spares -> ~103 GPUs -> ~7 racks of 16 GPUs each (or 12x8-GPU nodes depending on vendor)- Procurement note: large-model heavy deployments benefit from higher-memory GPUs (80GB+). Consider mixed fleet: 70% 80GB, 30% 40GB for cheap batch/rerank tasks.

Costing and tranche strategy (short):
- Stagger purchases into 3 tranches: proof-of-usage (20–30%), steady-state (40–50%), buffer and surge (20–30%).
- Always validate with a 90-day real-traffic run on the first tranche and update throughput_by_model_and_hw numbers before committing next tranche.
- Negotiate RMA and spare pool commitments with suppliers for lower operational risk.

Testing checklist (to run pre-order / pre-commit):
- Run synthetic mixed QPS with traffic shape from customer's telemetry (SRT distribution) and capture tail latencies.
- End-to-end control plane failover: drain pod, ensure autoredeploy pulls model images without exceeding OSS bandwidth caps.
- Pre-warm caches for top-100 prompts and evaluate hit ratios.
- Measure NVMe/model-pull times at 95th pctl.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Need better per-model token/sec calibration harness in CI that can run on small-scale cloud units.
- Validate egress estimation with an internal network profiler.
- Derive more robust batch_factor_estimate for mixed small/long request distributions.
- Confirm preferred node SKUs with procurement: vendor A has slightly cheaper list price but longer lead time.

References and pointers:
- CONFLUENCE: /display/ENG/Private+Deploy+Placement+Experiments  (see experimental charts)
- JIRA tickets listed above for rollout scripts and autoscaler tuning.

Misc notes (informal):
- If in doubt: increase headroom a little and avoid tight autoscale thresholds inside customer VPCs — noisy neighbors + cold-starts are the top root causes for latency SLO misses during early rollouts.
- Keep procurement tranches small for first-of-a-kind private fleets; we learned this the hard way on project 'Orion' where a single mis-estimate produced 30% overcommit.
